title: What Is a Heteronym? A Complete Guide with 50+ Examples
description: Heteronyms are words that share the same spelling but have different meanings and pronunciations. This comprehensive guide explains what makes them unique, how they differ from homonyms and homographs, and includes over 50 fascinating examples.

content.text: The English language is full of delightful quirks and linguistic oddities. One of the most fascinating is the heteronym — a word that's spelled exactly the same as another word but has a completely different meaning and often a different pronunciation.
Think about the word "lead." It can mean to guide someone ("I will lead the way") or refer to a heavy metal ("a lead pipe"). Same spelling. Different meanings. Different pronunciations.

A heteronym (also called a heterophone or, more technically, a homograph that is not a homophone) is a word that has the same spelling as another word but a different meaning and, crucially, a different pronunciation. The word comes from the Greek "hetero-" (different) + "-onym" (name). So literally: "different name."

Here's the key distinction: heteronyms are a subset of homographs. All heteronyms are homographs (same spelling), but not all homographs are heteronyms (some homographs share the same pronunciation — those are called homophones).
Heteronyms vs. Homonyms vs. Homographs vs. Homophones
These four terms are commonly confused. Let's break down the differences:

items.definition: Words that sound the same but have different meanings and spellings (e.g., "there" / "their" / "they're")
Words that are spelled the same but have different meanings (may or may not sound the same)
A broad category covering both homophones AND homographs — words that either sound the same or are spelled the same but have different meanings
A type of homograph — words spelled the same but with different meanings AND different pronunciations

Why Heteronyms Matter for Word Lovers

Heteronyms are more than just a linguistic curiosity. They reveal something profound about how language works: the same sequence of letters can encode completely different meanings depending on context. Your brain must parse the surrounding words to decide which meaning is intended — and it does this in milliseconds, usually without you even noticing.

This is what makes heteronyms such great material for word puzzles. Unlike Wordle (where you guess a word letter-by-letter), heteronym puzzles challenge your lateral thinking: given two seemingly unrelated clues, can you find the word that connects them?
